original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant k such that for every positive integer q one can choose an integer a coprime to q whose continued fraction expansion a/q = [b_0; b_1, ..., b_s] has all partial quotients bounded by k? The paper also records Zaremba's stronger original guess that k = 5.
target_in_paper: Zaremba's conjecture: the bounded-partial-quotients problem asking whether every positive denominator q occurs in a reduced fraction a/q whose regular finite continued fraction has uniformly bounded partial quotients, with Zaremba's original proposed bound equal to 5.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very well: it asks for a universal bound independent of q, quantifies over every positive integer q, requires a numerator a coprime to q, phrases the condition in terms of the continued fraction of a/q, and correctly notes the stronger original version with bound 5.
missing_details: The reduced fraction should be normalized by taking 1 <= a < q and gcd(a,q)=1, so that a/q lies in (0,1).
For that normalized fraction, the regular finite continued fraction is most naturally written a/q = [0; b_1, ..., b_s]; writing [b_0; ...] leaves an unnecessary ambiguity, since here b_0 = 0.
It should be explicit that the bound k (or M) is absolute/universal, i.e. independent of both q and the chosen a.
The partial quotients are positive integers in the ordinary regular continued-fraction expansion.
If one gives the equivalent set-theoretic reformulation, one should define Q_M := {q in N : there exists a with 1 <= a < q, gcd(a,q)=1, and all partial quotients of a/q are <= M}.
The draft is stand-alone mathematically, but it does not explicitly state that the conjecture concerns rational continued fractions over Q rather than arbitrary generalized continued fractions.
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute constant M such that for every positive integer q there is an integer a with 1 <= a < q and gcd(a,q)=1 for which the regular finite continued fraction of the reduced rational a/q, written a/q = [0; b_1, ..., b_s], has all partial quotients bounded by M (that is, b_j <= M for every j)? Equivalently, can one choose a universal bound on partial quotients that works for some reduced fraction with every denominator q? Zaremba's original form of the conjecture asks whether one may take M = 5.
equivalent_formulation: Let Q_M := {q in N : there exists an integer a with 1 <= a < q, gcd(a,q)=1, and every partial quotient in the regular finite continued fraction of a/q is at most M}. Then the question is whether Q_M = N for some absolute M; in Zaremba's original formulation, whether Q_5 = N.
justification: The draft is essentially the standard formulation of Zaremba's conjecture. The only real sharpening needed is to normalize the reduced rational to 0 < a/q < 1, which removes the distracting b_0 term and makes the regular expansion [0; b_1, ..., b_s] the natural paper-faithful form. The Q_M reformulation is the standard equivalent packaging used in nearby literature. I was able to confirm from an accessible OCR preview of arXiv:1202.4539 that this is indeed the survey on open problems in Diophantine approximation containing Littlewood's and Zaremba's conjectures, but the web-accessible preview truncates before the Zaremba section itself; so the refined wording above is sharpened using the standard later expositions of the same conjecture and its density-one partial result.
